terms.comment: The Latin word, made like sēmihōra; Columella uses it of a field and as an adjective, sēmicirculus ager.

terms.gloss: a semicircle; a semicircular seat or recess
evidence: Vitr. 9.7.3: ut aequa duo hēmicyclia sint dīvīsa
Cic. Amic. 2: domī in hēmicycliō sedentem
terms.comment: The Greek word, in Vitruvius for the figure, in Cicero and Pliny for a semicircular bench or garden end.

phrases.latin: Circulum per medium secā: fīent duo sēmicirculī.
phrases.english: Cut the circle down the middle: you’ll get two semicircles.

phrases.latin: Et per centrum perdūcendum, ut aequa duo hēmicyclia sint dīvīsa.
phrases.english: And a line must be drawn through the centre, so that it is divided into two equal semicircles.

phrases.latin: Omnis ager aut quadrātus, aut longus, aut cuneātus, aut triquetrus, aut rotundus, aut etiam sēmicirculī, vel arcūs, nōnnumquam etiam plūrimum angulōrum fōrmam exhibet.
phrases.english: Every field is square, or oblong, or wedge-shaped, or three-cornered, or round, or else has the shape of a semicircle or an arc, and sometimes even of a figure with many corners.

sources: Lewis & Short: semicirculus · Lewis & Short: hemicyclium · Lewis & Short: semiorbis
